From: Aaron Lowe <aaron.lowe@lumentech.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime feed: intermittent hangs and 502s on websocket

Neha —

We're hitting periodic streaming hangs on our LumenTech realtime pipeline during our evening peak (approx 23:30–00:30 UTC). Symptoms observed:
- Clients see a long silence (no tokens) for ~6–12s and then a burst of tokens (often duplicated).
- We see websocket disconnects with code 1006 and occasional 502/504 returned from your edge.
- During the window p95 token latency jumps from ~1.2s to 8–10s; error rate for streaming sessions increased to ~7% (baseline ~0.5%); throughput (successful session/min) down ~40%.

Attached are a handful of traces (request ids and timestamps). Customer impact: several live-monitor alerts and user-visible slowdowns in our product demo. We need an urgent triage and ETA — can you confirm whether this is a client-side backoff issue or something server-side?

Attaching: lumentech_sample_traces_20271012.log

Thanks,
Aaron Lowe

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime feed: intermittent hangs and 502s on websocket

Quick findings from the first sweep:
- Edge (AWS ALB) is logging a spike in connection resets aligned with the customer timestamps (~23:25 UTC). Reset rate jumped ~x6.
- NGINX proxies in the path show repeated chunked encoding flushes where the upstream connection is still open but the downstream buffer returned EPIPE.
- Series of 502s originate from our proxy pool that hit a short-lived threadpool starvation when inbound concurrency spikes — we observed a 30% CPU spin on a subset of pods.

Hypothesis: combination of ALB idle/keepalive mismatch + proxy buffering behavior causing partial-frame starvation and intermittent upstream resets. This manifests as long silent gaps followed by bursty output when the buffer is flushed.

Immediate mitigations proposed (low-risk):
1) Increase ALB idle timeout from 60s -> 120s for realtime listener (config change).
2) Disable proxy_buffering for the streaming route temporarily to avoid coalescing behavior.
3) Apply a runtime heartbeat (every 20s) from our serving runtime to ensure clients see periodic tokens.
4) Autoscaler: bring additional proxy pods online for the next 2 hours (manual scale to add headroom).

I’ve attached inf-8723 edge metrics snapshot (inf-8723-edge-metrics.png) and a short triage-runbook-20271013.pdf with rollback steps. Will start action 1 and 2 now.

—Rishi
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Realtime feed: intermittent hangs and 502s on websocket — resolution and next steps

Aaron / Sarah —

Thanks for your patience. Final update and root-cause summary:
What we saw: repeated short-lived connection resets at the ALB combined with proxy buffering behavior produced partial-frame starvation. In practice this caused long silent periods followed by token bursts when buffers flushed, plus a small set of 502s while the proxy threadpool hit transient contention under the spike.

What we changed (applied 13 Oct):
- ALB idle timeout increased 60s -> 120s for the realtime listener.
- Disabled proxy_buffering on the streaming route to avoid chunk coalescing.
- Deployed a runtime heartbeat patch that emits a lightweight keepalive token every 20s for streaming sessions.
- Manually scaled proxy pool and added +4 GPUs to Dedicated pool during the incident window.

Result: p95 token latency returned to baseline in subsequent peak windows (approx 24h of post-change monitoring). Error rate reduced to ~0.6%. Throughput returned to expected levels.

Next steps:
- Postmortem (INF-2027-8723) is queued for delivery by 2027-10-18 and will include long-term mitigations: smarter autoscaling thresholds, upgrade to keepalive-aware ALB config across customers, and a platform test that exercises sustained high-concurrency streaming to validate buffering behavior.
- We’ll schedule a short cross-functional call next week to review the postmortem and confirm whether LumenTech would like a credit; Marcus has pre-approved a one-off credit if impact >30 minutes.

Attachments: triage-runbook-20271013.pdf, lumentech_sample_traces_20271012.log

Apologies again for the disruption — let us know if you want a written status note for your users; we can send a joint update.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
